recent_posts.title: How to use Seedance 2.0 for AI video generation via Replicate
recent_posts.summary: Seedance 2.0 from ByteDance is a major leap in AI video generation, available via Replicate's API. Unlike typical video models, it accepts up to 9 images, 3 video clips, and 3 audio files as references alongside a text prompt, enabling character consistency, motion transfer, style referencing, and audio-driven rhythm. Audio and video are generated from a unified architecture for millisecond-level sync. The model supports up to 15 seconds of multi-shot output with camera planning, and responds to time-coded prompts specifying exact shot durations and transitions. Practical tips include overdescribing prompts, specifying camera movements, describing audio explicitly, and using 'hyper-realistic, 8k' as quality anchors. Python and JavaScript API examples are provided.

recent_posts.title: How to prompt Seedream 5.0 – Replicate blog
recent_posts.summary: Seedream 5.0 from ByteDance is an advanced image generation model with several standout capabilities: deep photographic and domain knowledge, example-based editing (show a before/after pair to teach transformations), multi-step logical reasoning, precise instruction following for complex compositions, strong text rendering (use double quotes for best results), and multi-image generation for cohesive sets. The post walks through each capability with detailed example prompts and results, and includes JavaScript and Python code snippets for using the model via the Replicate API. Key prompting tips include using natural language over keyword lists, specifying what to keep during edits, and using visual markers like bounding boxes for complex spatial instructions.

recent_posts.title: Recraft V4: image generation with design taste – Replicate blog
recent_posts.summary: Recraft V4 is a new image generation model available on Replicate in four variants: two raster (V4 and V4 Pro) and two vector (V4 SVG and V4 Pro SVG). Its standout features include 'design taste' — art-directed composition, integrated text rendering, and strong prompt accuracy up to 10,000 characters. Uniquely, the SVG models produce actual editable vector files with real paths and structured layers, compatible with Illustrator, Figma, and Sketch — not traced rasters. Code examples in JavaScript and Python show how to call all four models via the Replicate API with simple prompt, aspect_ratio, and size inputs.

recent_posts.title: Run Isaac 0.1 on Replicate – Replicate blog
recent_posts.summary: Isaac 0.1 is a 2B-parameter open-weight vision-language model designed for grounded perception tasks. It excels at OCR in challenging conditions, spatial reasoning, and visual question answering while providing bounding boxes to explain its answers. Despite its compact size, it rivals larger models in object recognition and visual reasoning. The model can learn new tasks from examples without fine-tuning and is optimized for real-time applications in robotics, manufacturing, and document processing. Available on Replicate's platform with a simple API for integration.

recent_posts.title: Run FLUX.2 on Replicate – Replicate blog
recent_posts.summary: Black Forest Labs released FLUX.2, an advanced AI image generation model available on Replicate in three variants: pro (6s generation, $0.015 base), flex (higher quality, 22s), and dev (open-source, 2.5s). The model generates photorealistic images up to 4MP with accurate rendering of hands, faces, and text. Key features include multi-reference support for up to 8 images with character consistency, direct pose control, hex-code color accuracy, and 32K prompt tokens. FLUX.2 improves upon FLUX.1 with better detail, text rendering, prompt following, and flexible output resolutions.

recent_posts.title: How to prompt Nano Banana Pro – Replicate blog
recent_posts.summary: Nano Banana Pro is a new image generation model with advanced capabilities including logical reasoning from text in images, accurate text rendering, character consistency across multiple reference images, and extensive world knowledge. The model can solve homework problems, render code accurately, maintain text adherence while applying creative styles, handle up to 14 reference images for character consistency, and create design mockups. It's available through Replicate's API with simple JavaScript integration.

recent_posts.title: Retro Diffusion's pixel art models are now on Replicate – Replicate blog
recent_posts.summary: Retro Diffusion's suite of four specialized AI models for generating pixel art is now available on Replicate. The models include rd-fast for quick generation, rd-plus for high-quality images, rd-tile for tilesets, and rd-animation for animated sprites. Each model supports multiple style presets and features like arbitrary dimensions, background removal, and seamless tiling, making them suitable for creating game assets, character sprites, maps, and UI elements.

recent_posts.title: Replicate is joining Cloudflare – Replicate blog
recent_posts.summary: Replicate, a platform for running AI models via API, has been acquired by Cloudflare. The service will continue operating as a distinct brand with the same API, while gaining access to Cloudflare's infrastructure and developer platform. Replicate provides abstractions for AI deployment, including Cog (an open-source tool for standardizing model formats) and a platform for sharing and running models. The integration aims to combine Replicate's AI primitives with Cloudflare's network infrastructure, Workers, Durable Objects, and other services to create a comprehensive platform for building AI applications.

recent_posts.title: Extract text from documents and images with Datalab Marker and OCR – Replicate blog
recent_posts.summary: Datalab's Marker and OCR models are now available on Replicate for document parsing and text extraction. Marker converts PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, and images into markdown or JSON, handling tables, math, code, and structured data extraction via JSON schemas. OCR detects text in 90 languages and returns reading order and table grids. Both models outperform established tools like Tesseract and GPT-4o, with Marker processing pages in 0.18 seconds and achieving 82.7% accuracy on olmOCR-Bench. Pricing starts at $2-6 per 1000 pages depending on mode and features.

recent_posts.title: How to prompt Veo 3.1 – Replicate blog
recent_posts.summary: Google's Veo 3.1 introduces advanced video generation features including reference-to-video (combining up to three images), first/last frame control for precise transformations, and enhanced image-to-video capabilities. The model supports cinematic prompting techniques for shot composition, camera movement, and lens effects. Fast generation options are available at half the cost with under 60-second processing times. The guide includes JavaScript API examples for basic image-to-video, multi-image reference generation, and frame interpolation workflows.
